Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported in
Sugar Land. Please state your full name for the record.
A: Sure. I'd rather keep my personal details out of it for now, but I'm the driver of the vehcile that was rear-ended.
Q: Understood. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Sugar Land, in the right lane, waiting to turn. I had been stopped for
maybe ten seconds when I felt a hard jolt from behind.
Q: What was the weather and road condition at the time?
A: It was clear and dry. Traffic was moderate, nothing unusual for that intersection.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?
A: Not really. I checked my mirror a moment before, but I didn't see it closing in. The impact came quickly.
Q: After the collision, did you feel any pain or discomfort?
A: Right away I had a stiff neck and a dull ache across the back of my shoulders. By the next morning, the pain had
moved up into the base of my skull and I had trouble turning my head to the left.
Q: Have you sought medical attention since the accident?
A: Yes, I was seen at an urgent care clinic the same evening and I've been going to a physical therapist twice a week
since then. The doctor diagnosed a neck strain and prescribed muscle relaxers and rest.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms today?
A: Yes, though it's improving slowly. Sitting at a desk for long periods still makes it worse, and I avoid lifting anything
heavy.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I'm happy to provide my treatment records once you need them.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
